subject: Transient p99 uplift — stratified routing proposal & customer timeline
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightCart SRE <eng@brightcart.com>, BrightCart PM <pm@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden p99 jump this afternoon — request for runbook and ETA

Hi Jonas,

We saw p99 latency for our GenAPI calls spike from ~380ms to ~2.1s starting ~16:45 UTC and it’s been intermittent since. Attach: traces and a sample request payload.

This is impacting Checkout recommendation freshness; we’ve throttled non-critical background calls but still seeing user-visible slowdowns. Can you share: 1) triage ETA; 2) immediate mitigation steps we can enable on our side; 3) expected timeline for any Redwood fix?

Thanks — Maria

--
Maria Lopez
Senior Engineering Manager, BrightCart
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 17:28:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p99 jump this afternoon — request for runbook and ETA

Team — forwarding BrightCart report + traces they attached. High priority. Initial look: traces show short-lived KV cache miss bursts combined with routing churn across replicas (region fallbacks). Marcus, can you run a quick check on per-replica queue depth? Karthik/Soojin, we should consider a routing stratification to isolate hot prefixes to warm RVs; this would be an exception but could stabilize p99 quickly.

Action asks:
- Marcus: per-replica QD + kernel scheduling snapshot (within 20m)
- Karthik: feasibility of on-the-fly routing stratification (roll forward within hours vs days)
- Soojin: customer comm draft once we have a mitigation plan (keep short + transparent)
- Marissa/Evelyn: business constraints (credits/SLA) if we propose route-exception that diverts capacity

I’ll triage the traces now and push any immediate hotfixes.

-Jonas
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 17:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 jump this afternoon — request for runbook and ETA

On Tue, Apr 16, 2029 at 17:28 Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus: per-replica QD + kernel scheduling snapshot (within 20m)

Taking the snapshot now — early signal: one replica in us-west-2 shows sustained KV cache misses correlated with a short GC spike on the allocator (saw ~120ms stalls) and a concurrent kernel switch to a quantized fallback path for a small subset of requests. Queue depth is elevated on that replica (avg qd 18 -> 46) while sibling replicas remain healthy (qd 6–10).

I pushed a temporary routing weight reduction for the impacted replica to 20% for BrightCart’s requests; that should reduce tail exposure while we investigate warmup behavior. I’ll attach logs.

Attachments: brightcart-replica-snap-20290416.log

-Marcus
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 18:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 jump this afternoon — request for runbook and ETA

Thanks for the data. Short answer: we can do a stratified routing roll for BrightCart that pins hot prefixes (identified by kernels/token-length signature) to a small set of warmed replica groups and keeps the remainder on standard routing. Implementation plan (fast path):

1) Identify hot prefixes via prefix-hash sampling (30m window) — Marcus has traces.
2) Create a temporary routing policy scoped to BrightCart that applies on their API key: route hot prefixes to warmed pool A (2x capacity) and fallback to pool B.
3) TTL the policy for 4 hours with automatic rollback if p99 not improved or if warm pool overloads.

Risk: diversion increases cost and may slightly increase p50 for some requests. Rollout time: ~1.5–3 hours if we accept manual approval for exception. I’ll need Marissa/Evelyn to sign off on the capacity/cost exception or confirm using burst reserves.

If approved, I’ll prepare the Playbook PDF (attached) + the minimal customer-facing note.

-Karthik
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 19:01:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 jump this afternoon — request for runbook and ETA

Approve the exception for BrightCart to use warmed pool A for the next 4 hours. Use reserved burst capacity; we’ll reconcile cost afterwards and flag under partner support. Evelyn — please confirm billing/credit stance for an identical incident during the quarter. Keep the customer note very clear: mitigation in place and we are monitoring; no SLA credit language unless we see recurrence.

Marissa
Product Lead, Inference Platform
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightcart.com>
Cc: BrightCart SRE <eng@brightcart.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 jump this afternoon — request for runbook and ETA

Maria — quick update and what we’ve done so far: 

1) We identified an elevated KV cache miss and a transient fallback to a quantized execution path on one replica in us-west-2 that correlated with p99 jumps.
2) We temporarily reduced routing weight to the impacted replica and enabled a scoped stratified routing policy for BrightCart that pins hot prefixes to warmed pool A. The policy is TTL’d for 4 hours starting 10:10 UTC.
3) We will monitor p99 and QD; Marcus has provided logs and is observing immediate p99 improvement in Canary traffic.

Expected customer impact: you should see p99 return toward baseline within minutes and remain stable while the policy is active. If anything changes we’ll escalate immediately.

Attachments: proposed-stratified-routing-playbook.pdf, brightcart-traces-20290416.json

Next steps:
- We’ll send a 1-line follow-up in 2 hours confirming stabilization.
- Karthik to open a postmortem JIRA (INF-8732) to root-cause and propose a longer-term fix (cache warmup + replica pre-warm).

Apologies for the disruption; we’ll keep iterating until stable.

-Jonas
